claims.text: Rapid nonequilibrium salt-melt synthesis creates a high density of grain boundaries in RuO2-based multielement oxides.
Multielement doping and grain boundaries act synergistically to tune the binding energies of oxygen intermediates.
The combined multielement and grain-boundary effects improve acidic OER activity and durability in RuO2-based catalysts.
Conventional slow cooling produces a lower grain-boundary density than rapid nonequilibrium quenching.
Fe, Co, Ni, and Ir can be incorporated into the RuO2 lattice through the nonequilibrium salt-melt synthesis.
Fe, Co, and Ni are introduced as activity-enhancing components, while Ir is introduced to improve acid resistance and stability.
Particle size and morphology should be held constant so that grain-boundary density is the principal structural variable in the comparison.
Grain boundaries create localized structural distortions or crystallographic misorientation.
Grain boundaries and external metal elements alter the electronic structure of RuO2.
The altered electronic structure and oxygen-intermediate binding energies change the OER reaction pathway.
A rapidly synthesized, grain-boundary-abundant catalyst will have lower OER overpotential than an equivalent-composition slow-cooled catalyst.
A rapidly synthesized, grain-boundary-abundant catalyst will have higher turnover frequency than an equivalent-composition slow-cooled catalyst.
A rapidly synthesized, grain-boundary-abundant catalyst will be more durable than an equivalent-composition slow-cooled catalyst.
The proposed mechanism should apply to RuO2-based or high-entropy oxide catalysts made by salt-melt synthesis under acidic water-splitting conditions.
Nanoparticle morphology and synthesis-induced defects other than grain boundaries may influence the measured performance.
The controlled comparison uses rapid-quenched and slow-cooled catalysts with identical chemical composition.

Failure of the grain-boundary-abundant catalyst to show any statistically significant improvement in overpotential, turnover frequency, or durability would falsify the proposed grain-boundary-governed enhancement.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as both inducing grain boundaries and incorporating additional dopants, whereas the baseline and falsification design require identical composition. It is therefore ambiguous whether both comparison samples contain the same dopants or whether composition changes along with synthesis route.
